title: All query categories served by one generic SQL tool
evidence: server.cpp:78 toolsList registers a single query_soccer tool; the five spec categories (match/team/player/competition/statistical) are satisfied via SQL over matches/performances/standings/derbies/players rather than dedicated semantic MCP tools
suggestion: No action needed — this is a valid, compact design; noted for cross-run comparison since other runs may expose per-category tools

title: Cup-final detection uses hard-coded round numbers per season
evidence: data.cpp:120 tags stage='final' via CASE season WHEN 2012 THEN 6 WHEN 2016 THEN 7 WHEN 2021 THEN 7 ELSE 8, and data.cpp:141-148 special-cases 2021-2023 reverse legs; seasons with a different final-round structure outside these would mis-tag
suggestion: Derive the final round from max(round) per season/competition, or document the covered seasons explicitly

title: Score reconciliation from extended file is heuristic (±1 day, name match)
evidence: data.cpp:126-138 backfills home_goal/away_goal from the extended table on competition+home+away within abs(julianday diff)<=1; README 'Coverage' discloses spelling differences and reschedules can affect reconciliation
suggestion: Acceptable given disclosure; aggregate stats over sparsely-reconciled seasons may be approximate

title: Integration tests rely on current working directory for data
evidence: test_soccer.py:11 spawns ['./soccer-mcp'] with no data-dir arg, relying on main() default 'data/kaggle' (server.cpp:135) resolving against cwd
suggestion: No action needed in-archive; the Makefile test target runs from the run dir where data/kaggle exists
